newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH CEZ TO DIVEST DISTRIBUTION - MINISTERS.
newsitem.headline: CZECH CEZ TO DIVEST DISTRIBUTION - MINISTERS.

text.p: The Czech council of economic ministers agreed on Tuesday that the main Czech power producer CEZ a.s. should divest its distribution assets by the year 2000, Industry and Trade Minister Karel Kuhnl told journalists.
"The council of ministers agreed that the distribution network should be separated from CEZ by the year 2000 through an agreement with CEZ," the minister told Reuters.
The decision must be approved by the full cabinet.
CEZ, in which the government still holds a two-thirds stake, is the largest power producer and controls much of the country's electricity distribution.
The government has been looking for ways to create more competition in the power industry.
Further details on how the seperation of CEZ's distribution network would take place have not been announced.
Earlier Kuhnl said that the council had agreed that energy deregulation should be completed by the year 2000 so that gas and electricity prices reflect their market costs.
